S110.01.note: The rich document editor opens only when the document round-trips as Markdown (ArtifactDocumentEditor.tsx:53-60); I did not find a visible save-as-new-version label, so the version step is unverified.
steps: Ask the assistant in chat to write a document, for example a short memo.
Click the document card under the reply so it opens in the artifact panel.
Click into the document text and change a sentence.

Open the artifact's menu and click Restore only if you need to compare versions; otherwise look for the edited text remaining after you close and reopen the panel, and check that a new version was recorded.
S110.01.where: Chat > open a document artifact from a reply (it opens in the artifact panel) > edit the text in the panel

S110.02.note: Searched apps/web/features/chat and apps/web/lib for a document-to-presentation control and found none; presentation artifacts exist (ArtifactPreview.tsx, title fallback 'Presentation') but no convert button. Production uploads also need UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:264-282).

S110.03.needs: a file to upload (an .xlsx); the sandbox path must be switched on by the owner (AGI_E2B_EXECUTION)
S110.03.note: Code audit says the chart path needs the E2B switch-on and the upload scanner; the attach control's visible word was not confirmed.
steps: Attach a spreadsheet (.xlsx) to a new chat message using the attach control in the composer.
Ask for an analysis with a chart, and a Word report that contains the chart.
When the report appears, open it in the artifact panel.
Open the artifact menu and click Download as Word (.docx); open the file and check that the chart is inside the report.
S110.03.where: Chat > attach an .xlsx file > ask for a chart inside a Word report > open the result in the artifact panel and choose Download as Word (.docx)

S110.05.note: The conversion is triggered by request wording (visual-intent.ts keywords); I found no dedicated one-step button.
steps: Ask the assistant for a research report on a topic and wait for it to finish.
In the next message, ask for the report as an interactive page with charts and navigation.
Open the page in the artifact panel and check that it has charts, navigation and controls.
Open the artifact's menu and click Publish; check that a link is produced.
S110.05.where: Chat > ask for a research report > ask for an interactive page from it > open the page in the artifact panel > Publish

S110.07.note: The voice-mode entry control's visible words were not confirmed in VoiceModeSurface.tsx.
steps: Start voice mode from the chat.
Say a task that needs a longer piece of work, for example a research summary.
Wait for the voice assistant to confirm it is starting a task.
Open Tasks in the sidebar and check that the task is listed and running in the background without you retyping it.
S110.07.where: Chat > voice mode > say a longer task out loud > Tasks in the sidebar

S110.08.note: Tool definition is in apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-tools.ts:135; the voice entry control's visible words were not confirmed.
steps: Start voice mode from the chat.
Say a request for a document, for example a Word file about a topic.
Wait until the document card appears in the voice session.
Open the document card and check that it opens as an artifact and can be downloaded.
S110.08.where: Chat > voice mode > ask for a document out loud > open the document from the voice session

S110.10.needs: an outside account (Google) with Gmail connected in Connectors
S110.10.note: Forwarded-email and address-based thread selection were not found in the code; the 'Schedules' entry word was not confirmed in the sidebar.
steps: Open the scheduled task page and open an existing scheduled task (or create one).
Find the trigger panel for the task and choose Gmail as the trigger type.
Read the note that says it runs for each new email and uses the Gmail address connected in Connectors.
Send a test email to the connected address and check that a tracked task run appears.
S110.10.where: Schedules > open a scheduled task > Triggers for <task name> > Gmail

S110.11.needs: a Slack workspace; the owner must switch the sandbox on (AGI_E2B_EXECUTION) before the coding session can run
S110.11.note: Slack settings exist in apps/web/features/settings/sections/SlackSection.tsx, but I found no visible path from a team mention to a coding session in /code; the feature depends on an owner switch-on.

S110.14.note: The Skills entry is in the shared settings navigation; the parent group heading was not checked.
steps: Finish a task in chat (for example a repeated process with clear steps).
Under the final reply, click Save as skill (or on a draft card, click Save as a skill).
Open Settings and choose Skills.
Find the new skill in the list and invoke it in a new chat to check that it runs.
S110.14.where: Chat > finish a task > under the reply click Save as skill, or on a plugin draft card click Save as a skill > Settings > Skills

S110.18.needs: a phone with the AGI mobile app signed in to the same account
S110.18.note: I checked the web sync route (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts) and the sidebar item, not the phone app code.
steps: On web or desktop, start a new chat and get one reply.
Open the AGI phone app with the same account and find the same chat in Chat history, with its full history.
On the phone, send a follow-up message.
Back on web, reload the chat and check that the phone's follow-up and its reply appear.
S110.18.where: Visible on the phone app's chat list and in the same chat on web; the phone side is outside this folder

S110.19.needs: the AGI command-line tool installed and a folder used in both places
S110.19.note: The terminal command name was not confirmed; the session list is in apps/web/features/code/components/LocalSessionsSection.tsx and its visible heading was not found.
steps: Start a coding session in a folder from the terminal with the AGI command-line tool.
Open the desktop app and click Code in the sidebar.
Choose the same folder; if asked, click Allow running commands.
Open the session listed for that folder and send a follow-up; check that it continues the terminal session.
S110.19.where: Code > choose the folder the CLI session used > open the CLI session from the list

S110.20.needs: VS Code installed; a folder with a desktop-app coding session
S110.20.note: Searched LocalSessionsSection.tsx, apps/cli and apps/desktop/electron for a visible VS Code or open-in-IDE control and found none by visible text.

S110.21.needs: a paired computer and a phone with the AGI app signed in to the same account
S110.21.note: I did not check whether a flag hides Remote Control in this build.
steps: On the computer, open Settings and choose Capabilities, then Remote Control, and pair the phone if it is not paired.
On the phone, send a new request to the paired computer.
On the computer, approve the request if an approval appears, and let the run finish.
On the phone, check that the result appears in the chat.
S110.21.where: Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control (pairing a phone); Linked devices lists paired computers

S110.24.needs: a project with sources and instructions
S110.24.note: The picker's visible words were not confirmed; the label above is the picker's project label in the code.
steps: In a new chat, open the project picker in the composer.
Choose the project that holds the notebook's instructions and sources.
Ask a question that the project's sources cover.
Check that the answer uses the project's sources and instructions.
S110.24.where: Chat > composer > Project picker > choose a project > ask a question in that chat

S110.25.note: The answer menu's trigger word was not confirmed; the save label is in MessageBubble.tsx.
steps: Open a conversation with an answer you want to keep.
On the answer, open its menu and click Save to project.
Pick the project name in the list.
Open the project and check Project sources; then start a chat in that project and ask about the saved answer.
S110.25.where: Chat > an answer's menu > Save to project > choose the project; then open the project and check Project sources

S110.26.needs: an account whose usage is used up (for example a Free account)
S110.26.note: The labels are built from code templates, and the usage-block switch is in apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx; how to reach the limit was not confirmed.
steps: Send messages until a usage limit blocks a send.
Read the card under the composer and check which options it offers.
Click Switch to <model name> if it is offered (or Buy credits or Upgrade to).
Check that the chat continues and the reply comes from the new model.
S110.26.where: Chat > send a message after usage is used up > the paywall card under the composer > Switch to <model name>, Buy credits or Upgrade to <plan>

S110.28.needs: a published artifact on the account
S110.28.note: PublishedArtifactsSection.tsx has a Published artifacts heading and a live-again message, but no settings nav entry for it was found in packages/ui/ui/src/settings-nav.ts or apps/web/features/settings/components/web-settings-navigation.ts; the republish control is Publish in ArtifactPreview.tsx.

labels.text: Save a copy to my chats

S110.29.needs: a second account and a shared link from the first account
S110.29.note: The label is a fallback string in a translation call; the shared-conversation path (apps/web/app/chat/from-share/[token]/page.tsx) was not walked through.
steps: Sign in with a second account (not the owner).
Open a public or shared artifact link created by the first account.
Click Save a copy to my chats.
Open My chats and check that the copy opens with the same content and can be continued.
S110.29.where: Open a shared artifact link from another account > Save a copy to my chats

S110.30.needs: a workspace with a second member in the same workspace; sharing rights depend on the member's role
S110.30.note: The link from Settings to /workspace/sharing was not confirmed; the sharing section is mounted by apps/web/app/workspace/sharing/page.tsx.
steps: Open Settings and choose Workspace.
Find the sharing section and click Share project with organization on one of your projects, with an access level if asked.
Sign in as a second member of the same workspace and find the shared item under Shared with your organization.
Open it and check that it opens with the access level you chose.
S110.30.where: Settings > Workspace > Share project with organization (sharing page at /workspace/sharing)
